text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel will pay a two-day visit to Slovakia, starting May 1. Kinkel is scheduled to meet Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, his Slovak counterpart Pavol Hamzik and Parliamentary Chairman Ivan Gasparovic. The talks will include Slovakia's integration into western structures.
- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin will visit on April 24 and 25. He is expected to sign 10 unspecified treaties aimed to boost Slovak-Russian cooperation.

- The paper quotes unnamed sources as saying the Slovak branch of the Czech bank Agrobanka has been bought by a group of Slovak firms closely linked to the ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS).
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - An unspecified EU document warns that Slovakia's economy is becoming overheated, saying the worsening country's balance of payment was the most concerning issue.

- The state-owned Slovak Railways (ZRS) said it had yet to calculate losses caused by a recent strike of Czech rail workers, but added that the sum "will definitely exceed 50 million crowns." ZRS will demand compensation from Czech railways.
- The judges of the International Court of Justice on Thursday leave Slovakia and will continue their inspection of the controversial Gabcikovo dam from the Hungarian side.
- State-owned gas distributor SPP said its 1996 pre-tax profit totalled 13.8 billion crowns.
- Slovakia's major paper and pulp producer JCP Sturovo has called an annual shareholders meeting for May 7.
SME - Former Foreign Minister Eduard Kukan said Slovakia had "no chance" of being elected to the post chairman of the UN General Assembly. Slovakia's candidate is foreign minister Pavol Hamzik.
